### Sunday Closes With More Than 1,600 Flights Cancelled and the Full Return Moved to Monday, the Gulf Closes Ranks Behind Bahrain While Washington Files No Word on the Radar, and the Petition to Bring Back Mr. Huang Passes 154,000 With No Answer From the Board

Filed as: Edition No. 52 — The Evening Watch · 2026-11-15T18:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-15-evening-watch.html

The Evening File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Sunday Closes With More Than 1,600 Flights Cancelled and the Full Return Moved to Monday, the Gulf Closes Ranks Behind Bahrain While Washington Files No Word on the Radar, and the Petition to Bring Back Mr. Huang Passes 154,000 With No Answer From the Board

 The evening file: a recovery day that ended smaller than Saturday and larger than promised, with its cause named to a town in Arkansas; a morning of drones in the Gulf answered in writing by five capitals and not answered by a sixth; a count that spent Sunday where Saturday left it; a spokesman’s two sentences repeated to the evening wires; a petition that grew by tens of thousands while its board said nothing; and a week ahead written entirely in dates.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1800 ET, Sunday, November 15, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 50, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 today, from Edition No. 49, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, from Edition No. 48, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, and from Edition No. 47, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Saturday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the evening figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Evening in Brief: The Day Whole, and the First Considered Responses From Every Side

Sunday’s developments, whole, are a recovery that did not finish, a claim that gained responses without gaining confirmation, and a set of counts that moved everywhere except in Alaska. More than 1,600 flights were cancelled and nearly 3,600 delayed on Sunday in the wire account filed below, nearly 1,700 had been cancelled by 1350 in the tracker account filed below, and more than 17,000 flights have been scrubbed since Friday in the same account; the Secretary’s Sunday version of the promise, back to normal today and probably fully normal tomorrow, is the version the day bore out, and the cause file gained its place in the El Dorado account filed below. In the Gulf, the considered responses arrived: Manama’s statement stands in the ministry account filed below, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned the attacks in the condemnations account filed below, Tehran’s spokesman defended the strikes as self-defence in the accounts filed below, and no American word on Sunday’s radar claim stands in any account the desk read by 1800. In Alaska no new count came on Sunday; the state’s Saturday report stands at 140,637 to 129,424, and the race stands uncalled. In Nvidia’s file the petition’s counter passed 154,000 and kept rising, and the board filed no public answer. The evening’s other files, Moscow’s two sentences, Shenzhen’s two confirmations and one silence, France’s two counts and Spain’s new tracking, stand below in their places.

The Airlines at Evening: More Than 1,600 Cancelled, a Router at El Dorado, and the Promise Settled on Tomorrow

The recovery’s final shape for Sunday is a system working and a schedule still short. More than 5,200 flights were affected on Sunday in the wire account above, which counts more than 1,600 cancelled and almost 3,600 delayed, against more than 6,400 cancelled and more than 8,000 delayed on Saturday; the tracker account above counts nearly 1,700 cancelled and 5,280 delayed by 1350, and a third account counts more than 5,000 delayed and a further 2,000 cancelled in the day. The desk prints the three counts apart in the Cocked Hat; they were taken at different hours by different counters, and they agree on the order of the day, a third day of disruption far below Saturday and far above a normal Sunday. The shares stand where midday left them: JetBlue cancelled 27 percent of its Sunday operation and American 13 percent, with Southwest, United and Delta at 3 to 5 percent, in the wire account. Monday’s cancellations stood at 33 by Sunday afternoon in the tracker account, against fewer than 30 in the morning; the smallness of that figure is the recovery’s best evidence.

The cause file gained a town, a pair of routers, and an open question. Secretary Duffy said on Sunday that a newly installed router at a remote Administration site in El Dorado, Arkansas, started flooding the network during work by the contractor L3Harris on a copper-to-fiber upgrade, in the El Dorado account above; both routers are now with the contractor, Administration staff are on site, the Federal Bureau of Investigation is offering support, and officials still do not know whether the fault lay with the equipment or with the contractor that installed it, in the same account. The Secretary’s earlier sentence stands beside it: the system did not meet the moment, the contractor did not meet the moment, or the equipment did not. Administrator Bedford’s Saturday promise, full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday, was not met in the form stated; the Secretary’s Sunday form, fully normal tomorrow, is now the standing promise, and Monday will be read against it. No sign of a cyberattack stands in any account in the file.

Bahrain at Evening: Five Capitals Answer in Writing, Tehran Answers Back, and Washington Does Not Answer

The first considered responses to Sunday’s morning are regional, written, and aligned. Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry said the attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighbourliness and stressed an immediate halt, in the condemnations account above; Qatar’s Foreign Ministry called the continuation of the attacks a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavours, in the same account; Jordan and Egypt condemned the attacks and expressed solidarity with Bahrain, in the same account and in the second-attack account filed below. Manama’s own statement, in the ministry account above, holds Iran fully responsible, rejects the transformation of Bahraini territory into an arena for settling scores, cites Security Council Resolution 2817 and Bahrain’s right of self-defence under Article 51, in coordination with the Gulf Cooperation Council under its joint defence agreement, and calls on the Security Council, where Bahrain sits, to condemn the attacks and take decisive measures. The Defence Force’s account stands: its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks before they reached their targets, in the Bahrain account filed below.

Tehran’s answer and Washington’s silence complete the evening file. The Guards say six drones of their Aerospace Force targeted the American air-defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base, in a second phase of retaliation, in the Bahrain account above and in the drone account filed below; no damage and no casualties have been reported, and neither Washington nor Manama has confirmed a hit. Tehran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman, Mr. Baghaei, defended the strikes at a news conference as justified in self-defence and said Iran would keep responding to military aggression by the United States or other states, in the second-attack account above; Article 51 is therefore claimed in the same file by Manama for its defence and by Tehran for its strikes, for opposite acts, and the desk prints both claims as claims. Central Command, which denied Friday’s claim in claim-and-fact form, had filed no word on Sunday’s claim in any account the desk read by 1800, and the desk records the silence as a fact of the file, not as an answer. The President’s Saturday condition, that he might hold off on attacking Iran if there were no new provocations, stands unapplied to Sunday’s claim in any statement in the file.

The Count at Evening: No Sunday Count, 157 Short of a Majority, and Three Dates Left in November

Alaska’s Senate count spent Sunday exactly where Saturday afternoon left it, and the desk prints it whole one more time. The state’s unofficial summary, timed 1515 on Saturday, gives Ms. Peltola 140,637 votes, 49.94 percent; Senator Sullivan 129,424, 45.96 percent; Mr. Heikes 6,002; Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. 4,652; and write-ins 872, on 281,587 votes in the race, with 283,618 ballots cast and all 401 precincts reported, in the state’s report filed below. The lead is 11,213; a majority of the reported vote is 140,794, and Ms. Peltola stands 157 votes short of it by the desk’s arithmetic. The Press estimates 97 percent counted and has not called the race, in the midday file; one tracker lists a winner, Ms. Peltola declared victory on Saturday, the President declared Senator Sullivan the winner on November 7, and Senator Sullivan has not conceded, in the ballot account and the lead account filed below, which record that the latest batch added 2,397 votes for Ms. Peltola and 1,596 for Senator Sullivan and that leaders held in all three statewide races. The next count is due Monday; overseas ballots may arrive through Wednesday, November 18, when the ranked-choice tabulation is scheduled if no candidate holds a majority; certification is targeted for November 25.

Dublin and Shenzhen at Evening: Two Sentences Repeated, and a Departure in the Morning

Europe’s file closed Sunday as it opened, with one spokesman’s two answers carried by the evening wires. Asked by the TASS agency whether Europe’s negotiators have attempted to contact Russia, spokesman Peskov answered, “No, not yet,” in the contact account filed below; in an interview with a Vesti correspondent he said that in the absence of a negotiated solution Russia will have to achieve its objectives by force, and that if the Union does not want peace there is no point in discussing a settlement or a European security framework, in the force account filed below. No European answer to either sentence stands in the evening file, and no date for a first contact stands in it. The standing American sentence, that the delegation at Abu Dhabi ensured Europe will be included in future talks, stands where the week left it.

Shenzhen gained no third confirmation on Sunday and gained a clock. The meeting of the three presidents on Thursday, November 19, stands confirmed by the White House on Friday and by the Kremlin on Saturday, and unconfirmed by its host, in the meeting account and the agenda account filed below; China’s Friday sentence, that it is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state, stands unamended at 1800. The agenda split stands whole: nuclear arms and Iran in the American telling, with no agreement expected in the same telling; Ukraine off the trilateral agenda in the American telling and on it in the Kremlin aide’s. The President departs Monday for Manila and the ASEAN meetings and continues to Shenzhen, due there November 17 through 19, in the same accounts. Monday’s departure is the next fact in the file.

Nvidia at Evening: A Counter Past 154,000, a Board That Has Not Answered, and a Report of a War Room

The petition’s day is a rising counter and a standing silence. The counter read 154,678 names at 1001 Pacific on Sunday, up from 117,112 at 1403 Pacific on Saturday, in the petition account filed below, which breaks the total down as 7,459 self-described current employees, 1,406 former employees, 81,896 shareholders and 63,917 other supporters, and records in the same file that the affiliations are self-reported and not verified and that fake entries appeared among the names. A later account puts the counter at 156,850, with more than 7,500 current employees, in the comeback account filed below, which reports that Mr. Huang has discussed a return with confidants and that allies are assembling a lobbying effort on his behalf; a third account puts the total at 151,083, in the finance account filed below. The petition’s asks stand in all the accounts, in the campaign account filed below: reinstatement while an independent investigation establishes the facts, the investigation’s scope, independence and timetable made public, a substantive opportunity to respond, and, if the board insists he leave, a specific, evidence-backed explanation. The board had not publicly responded to the petition or to the Gerstner and Baker letter in any account the desk read by 1800; its succession file stands at choosing a search firm, with an approach to an outside candidate reported and no engagement made. No finding has been made by the board, by any committee or by any court on any allegation in this file. Earnings stand on Tuesday, November 17, after the close, with consensus revenue at $108.9 billion against the company’s outlook of $108.0 billion in the week’s file.

The Markets at Evening: A Sunday Read in One Open Market, and Futures at 1800

Sunday has no cash session, and the evening reading is Friday’s closes, the weekend’s one open market, and the hour now at hand. Friday’s closes stand: the S&P 500 at 7,561.67, down 0.40 percent; the Nasdaq Composite at 25,136.27, down 0.91; the Dow at 52,347.60, up 0.10; the ten-year yield at 5.15 percent; the dollar index at 103.41. Bitcoin traded at $64,502 at 1738 UTC on Sunday, 6.3 percent below its Friday close, after a low of $61,946 in the night, in the week-ahead account filed below; at $65,025 in an afternoon reading and at $65,570 at 0845 after a low of $62,006, the lowest since July, in the bitcoin account filed below; and above $65,000 in a late account that counts about $808 million of futures liquidations in the 24 hours to Sunday, in the accounts filed below. The Fear and Greed reading stood at 10 on Sunday against 20 on Friday, in the week-ahead account. Futures reopen at 1800 today, the hour of this collection; their first readings belong to the Midnight Watch. The week’s calendar is dated in every file: retail sales and Nvidia on Tuesday, the October meeting minutes on Wednesday, the Anthropic listing on Thursday in one account and its pricing on Wednesday in another, printed apart in the Cocked Hat.

France and Spain at Evening: A Bill Dated November 19 in Paris, and a New Tracking in Spain

France’s fifth Saturday gained its Senate date on Sunday. The Interior Ministry’s count stands at 106,000 nationwide, 24,000 in Paris, down from 146,000 the Saturday before, with 219 detained in the week’s file; the organisers’ count stands at about 200,000, almost 100,000 in the capital, in the demonstrations account filed below, which records a range of demands, from protecting children and increasing wages to more resources for education and protest against the police bill. That bill, giving officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms and called a licence to kill by its critics in the accounts, is scheduled to be examined by the Senate on November 19, in the same account and in the Senate account filed below. The unions’ Tuesday strike stands, called after the government’s 0.6 percent minimum-wage promise was rejected; Tuesday is also the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vest movement, and a sixth Saturday is called for November 21.

Spain’s campaign gained a tracking and kept its divided polls. The first instalment of a new tracking, published Sunday, puts the Popular Party at 30.8 percent and 130 seats, the Socialists at 26.4 percent and 106 seats, and Vox at 18.2 percent and 65 seats, a combined 195 seats for the first and third parties against 176 needed for a majority, in the tracking account filed below. The mean of sixteen institutes stands at Popular Party 31.4, Socialists 26.9, Vox 19.1, Frente Amplio 6.3 and ERC 2.5, in the campaign account filed below; the state survey’s Socialist lead stands against both figures in the file where the week left it. Mr. S&aacute;nchez opened in Seville, Mr. Feij&oacute;o in Badalona, and Mr. Abascal and the Frente Amplio candidates in Madrid, in the same account; a head-to-head television debate is reported set for November 19, and polls may publish until November 23. Spain votes on November 29.

The Week Ahead: Every File in This Edition Is Dated

Monday carries the recovery’s verdict, the President’s departure, and Alaska’s next count. The airlines will be read against the Secretary’s fully-normal-tomorrow promise and Monday’s 33 cancellations counted on Sunday afternoon. Alaska’s count resumes Monday ahead of Wednesday’s tabulation. Tuesday carries retail sales, France’s strike, and Nvidia’s earnings after the close. Wednesday carries the October meeting minutes, the APEC leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen, and Alaska’s tabulation. Thursday carries the three presidents in Shenzhen and the Senate’s examination of the police bill in Paris. Spain votes November 29; Mr. Huang’s interview stands dated December 1; the Federal Reserve decides December 8 and 9. The Midnight Watch collects at 0000.

The Cocked Hat

Where the evening’s bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On Sunday’s cost: more than 1,600 cancelled and nearly 3,600 delayed in the wire count, nearly 1,700 cancelled and 5,280 delayed by 1350 in the tracker account, more than 5,000 delayed and a further 2,000 cancelled in a third account, and 1,606 cancelled at 1100 in the El Dorado account—readings taken at different hours, agreeing on the day’s order and on nothing finer. On the promise: full schedule integrity by the close of business Sunday in the Administrator’s Saturday words, fully normal tomorrow in the Secretary’s Sunday words, and a day that met neither in full and the second in prospect. On the failed thing: a router at El Dorado flooding the network in the Secretary’s Sunday account, with equipment failure and installer error both open. On Bahrain: intercepts and destruction in the Defence Force’s account, six drones on target in the Guards’, condemnations from four neighbouring capitals, Article 51 claimed by both sides, and no confirmation of a hit and no American word from any capital. On Alaska’s share: 49.94 percent on the state’s full denominator, 50.1 on the dashboard that excludes unresolved write-ins, a winner listed on one tracker, no call from the Press, a victory declared by one candidate and a winner declared by the President for the other. On Europe: not yet contacted in the spokesman’s answer, included in future talks in the White House’s November 13 sentence, and objectives by force absent a negotiated solution in the spokesman’s interview, with no European answer in the evening file. On Shenzhen: confirmed by Washington and Moscow, unconfirmed by its host, with Ukraine on the agenda in one capital’s telling and off it in another’s. On the petition: 151,083, 154,678 and 156,850 in three Sunday readings of one counter, its affiliations self-reported, its fake entries named in its own accounts, and no answer from its board. On bitcoin: $61,946, $62,006, $64,502, $65,025 and $65,714 in readings taken at five hours of a Sunday. On France: 106,000 in the Ministry’s count and about 200,000 in the organisers’. On Spain: 30.8 percent for the Popular Party in the new tracking, 31.4 in the sixteen-institute mean, and a Socialist lead in the state survey. Inside the triangle is where the evening honestly stands.

 The Clippings Filed With This Edition

 Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 27 items.

 

 SubjectiveReuters via Virginia Business — more than 1,600 cancelled and almost 3,600 delayed on Sunday, and a return to normalcy predicted by MondayUnited States air travel disruptions continued for a third day on Sunday with more than 5,200 flights already affected, but the Transportation Secretary predicted a return to normalcy by Monday as airlines scrambled to get back on schedule after a systemwide ground stop. More than 1,600 flights nationwide were cancelled and almost 3,600 were delayed on Sunday, according to FlightAware; airlines on Saturday had cancelled more than 6,400 flights and delayed more than 8,000. The Secretary said flights will come back to normal on Sunday but probably fully normal on Monday, and emphasised the Administration’s focus on keeping passengers safe. On Sunday 27 percent of JetBlue flights and 13 percent of American Airlines flights were cancelled, with Southwest, United and Delta reporting cancellations of 3 to 5 percent of their flights. The Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours.

 SubjectiveThe Points Guy — nearly 1,700 cancelled by 1350 Sunday, more than 17,000 scrubbed since Friday, and 33 of Monday’s downSunday was shaping up to be another rough day at airports across the country, with travellers facing a third straight day of widespread cancellations after Friday’s nationwide ground stop. As of 1:50 p.m. Eastern on Sunday, nearly 1,700 flights had been cancelled and another 5,280 had been delayed, according to FlightAware; all told, more than 17,000 flights have been scrubbed since Friday. Cancellations appeared to slow entering Sunday compared with the past two days, but operations had not returned to normal, especially on some carriers. The Administrator had said disruptions were expected to begin easing by Sunday evening, and that the airline partners believe they will be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. As of Sunday afternoon, 33 flights for Monday had been cancelled, a total that had not increased much since the morning, suggesting operations may be stabilising. The account records the ground stop’s cause as a communications outage affecting air traffic control discovered late Friday afternoon.

 SubjectiveUSA Today — more than 1,600 cancelled and almost 4,200 delayed in the updated count, and the system stableUnited States air travel remained disrupted as of midday on November 15 after more than 15,000 flights were cancelled in the last two days following the nationwide ground stop. More than 1,600 flights within, into or out of the United States were cancelled and almost 4,200 were delayed on Sunday, according to FlightAware. The Transportation Secretary said flights will come back to normal on Sunday but probably fully normal on Monday, and emphasised the Administration’s focus on keeping passengers safe. As of the morning of November 15, the Administration’s National Airspace System dashboard reported no active en-route events, a strong indication the communications failure is no longer constraining the national system; local traffic management programs are still possible later today in eight named areas, as airport and route-specific contingencies and not another nationwide ground stop. On November 13 about 9,200 flights were cancelled and 7,500 delayed after essentially all departures were halted for nearly five hours. The Secretary said on November 14 that the preliminary investigation points to work by the contractor L3Harris during a routine upgrade from copper wiring to fiber.

 SubjectiveSourceFirst News — the El Dorado, Arkansas router, 1,606 cancelled by 1100, and a full return that could slip into MondayFriday’s nationwide ground stop began when a newly installed router at a remote Administration site in El Dorado, Arkansas, started flooding the air traffic control network, the Transportation Secretary said on Sunday; officials still do not know whether the fault lay with the equipment or with the contractor that installed it. Both routers are now with L3Harris, the contractor that owns and operates the network, while Administration staff are on site and the Federal Bureau of Investigation is offering support. As investigators examine the Arkansas router, FlightAware counted 1,606 United States flight cancellations by 11 a.m. Eastern on Sunday, against 6,696 for all of Saturday, and 3,343 delayed. The Administration’s airport status feed showed no ground stop anywhere at 11 a.m. The Administrator had promised on Saturday that schedules would be back to normal by the close of business Sunday; on Sunday the Secretary moved that toward Monday, saying planes and crews were still out of position and that by the end of the day and into tomorrow the system should be running at full capacity.

 SubjectiveWashington Post account — airlines scramble to resume flights, with the two promises printed side by sideAirlines scrambled on Sunday to return flight schedules to normal by the evening, two days after a nationwide ground stop triggered widespread cancellations and delays across the United States. While thousands of flights were disrupted over the weekend, with over a thousand more cancellations reported on Sunday, airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crews, after officials expressed confidence that the worst of the disruption is over. The Transportation Secretary told a Sunday programme that things will come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow; the Administrator said airlines expect they will be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. FlightAware reported more than 6,600 flights cancelled on Saturday, with at least 1,300 additional cancellations recorded early Sunday. American Airlines said all planned cancellations for Saturday night and Sunday had been completed, although some individual flights could still be cancelled as it works to restore operations. The outage was believed to have been caused by problems during maintenance at a remote site, where a contractor was replacing old copper telecommunications lines with fiber-optic cables.

 SubjectiveCrisis Zone — Bahrain says it destroyed Iranian aerial attacks as Tehran claims a radar strikeBahrain’s Interior Ministry issued its first threat alerts since September, naming no threat, while explosions were heard in Manama; the Defence Force then said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks. The Guards said six drones targeted an American air-defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base; no damage or casualties had been reported, and neither American nor Bahraini authorities had confirmed any hit. The Guards’ statement was carried by the state broadcaster’s channel, by Fars and by Press TV. Friday’s claim was denied by Central Command, which said two drones were shot down with no injuries or damage. The account records the President’s Saturday condition, that he might hold off on attacking Iran if there were no new provocations from Tehran or the Houthis, and that he would maintain the naval blockade.

 SubjectiveFana News — Bahrain strongly condemns Iran’s continued attacks, citing Resolution 2817 and Article 51Bahrain has condemned, in the strongest terms, Iran’s continued attacks on its territory after air defence systems intercepted and destroyed drones launched on Sunday, two days after intercepting two others in a similar attack. The Foreign Ministry described the attacks as a resumption of Iran’s aggression against Bahrain and regional countries, in blatant disregard for international law and the Charter; a flagrant violation of Security Council Resolution 2817, which condemned Iranian attacks on Bahrain and neighbouring countries and demanded their immediate cessation; and a foreclosing of de-escalation efforts imperilling regional security and stability. The ministry affirmed Bahrain’s inherent individual and collective right to self-defence under Article 51 and to take all necessary measures to safeguard its sovereignty and the security of its citizens and residents. As a member of the Security Council, Bahrain called on the Council to condemn the repeated attacks, shoulder its responsibilities, and take decisive measures to ensure Iran’s full compliance with Resolution 2817.

 SubjectiveThe Guardian live account via The Bull Post — Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemn the attack, with Manama’s full statementSaudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt have all strongly condemned the Iranian attack on Bahrain and expressed solidarity with the kingdom, in statements carried by Bahrain’s news agency. Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry affirmed that the attacks constitute a violation of international law and the principles of good neighbourliness, and stressed the importance of an immediate halt and of serious steps towards security and stability for the region and its peoples. Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said the continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that will complicate efforts to contain the tension and undermine political and diplomatic endeavours aimed at achieving security and stability. The account reproduces Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry statement in full: the strongest condemnation of continued aggression, drones intercepted and destroyed on Sunday and two on Friday, a flagrant violation of Resolution 2817, rejection of the Guards’ pretexts, rejection of the transformation of Bahraini territory into an arena for settling scores, Iran held fully responsible, Article 51 self-defence in coordination with the Gulf Cooperation Council under its joint defence agreement, and a call for the Security Council to act.

 SubjectiveKhabarWire — Iran strikes a Bahrain air base for a second time in days, and the Gulf closes ranksThe Guards said they launched six drones at an American air-defence radar at al-Riffa air base in Bahrain before dawn on Sunday, the second attack on the kingdom in three days; Bahrain’s Defence Force said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks before they reached their targets, and the Interior Ministry issued two public alerts telling residents to seek shelter. The attack came shortly after 4 a.m. local time, with residents reporting a second series of blasts around 6:30. Bahrain’s Foreign Ministry expressed the kingdom’s strongest condemnation, described the attack as a violation of Resolution 2817, said no pretext could justify aggression against a state’s sovereignty, rejected the transformation of its territory into an arena for settling scores, held Iran responsible, and invoked Article 51 and the Cooperation Council’s joint defence agreement. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned the attack; Saudi Arabia called it a violation of international law and good neighbourliness, and Qatar called the continuation a dangerous escalation. Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesman defended the attack as justified under Article 51 because those states had aided American operations against Iran. No independent assessment of what was targeted or damaged has been published, and the American military had not commented on Sunday’s attack when the account was written.

 SubjectiveBrussels Reporter — Iranian drones target an American air-defence radar site in BahrainIran launched a drone attack on an American military base in Bahrain on Sunday, the second attempt to target the country in three days, as tensions over the Strait of Hormuz continue. The Guards said they targeted an American air-defence radar facility at al-Riffa air base with six drones. Bahrain’s military said its air defence systems intercepted and destroyed the incoming drones before they could achieve their objectives. The attack followed an Iranian drone strike on Bahrain on Friday, the first against Gulf countries since September.

 SubjectiveLaPresse — the Kremlin says European negotiators have not yet contacted RussiaThe negotiators appointed by the European Union have not yet attempted to contact Russia, the Kremlin’s spokesman said in response to a question from the TASS agency. “No, not yet,” the spokesman said. At the informal European summit in Dublin, the heads of state and government opted for a format that includes the European institutions and the five countries, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy and Poland, alongside the Commission and the Council, to represent Europe in the negotiations on Ukraine.

 SubjectiveLaPresse — the Kremlin says that without an agreement with Europe, Russia will have to use forceIn the absence of a negotiated solution with Europe, Russia will have to achieve its objectives by force, the Kremlin’s spokesman said in an interview with a Vesti correspondent, according to reports from Russian news agencies. The spokesman said that for Moscow the resolution of the conflict in Ukraine is inextricably linked to the new European security architecture, and that in the absence of any room for negotiation, Russia will have to do so by force. Earlier, the spokesman had told TASS that the negotiators chosen by Europe had not yet attempted to establish contact with Russia.

 SubjectiveCNN — the President to meet with China’s and Russia’s leaders at a trilateral sit-down on nuclear non-proliferationThe President will meet jointly next week with China’s leader and Russia’s President, the White House said on Friday, a first-ever trilateral sit-down between the leaders of the three countries. The meeting, on the sidelines of the APEC summit in China, will focus on nuclear non-proliferation, a topic the President has said he believes could yield a new agreement between the world’s biggest nuclear-armed states. The Kremlin says the meeting will take place on November 19 in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, but there has been no confirmation yet from China. The last nuclear arms treaty between the United States and Russia expired in February.

 SubjectiveSilent Dossier — the Kremlin confirms the Shenzhen meeting as Washington keeps Ukraine off the agendaThe Kremlin confirmed on Saturday, November 14, that the three presidents will meet in Shenzhen on November 19; Ukraine is not on the agenda of that meeting, a senior American official told reporters on Friday, and China is silent. The Kremlin’s spokesman said an agreement has been reached to hold a trilateral meeting on the 19th in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the APEC summit, and gave no agenda. China, the host, has confirmed nothing; its Foreign Ministry said on Friday only that it is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state. American officials said the President will raise nuclear arms and Iran, and that they expect no nuclear agreement; a Kremlin aide said on November 12 that the Ukraine settlement would be discussed with the President in Shenzhen. No separate meeting between the American and Russian presidents is scheduled; the American President is due to hold a bilateral meeting and a working lunch with China’s leader on Thursday before the trilateral session, and APEC’s leaders’ meeting is held in Shenzhen on November 18 and 19 with China’s leader in the chair.

 SubjectiveImplicator — the petition to bring back Mr. Huang tops 150,000 names, at 154,678 on Sunday morningThe petition counter read 154,678 names at 10:01 a.m. Pacific on Sunday, November 15, up from 117,112 at 2:03 p.m. Pacific on Saturday. The campaign asks Nvidia’s board to restore its co-founder as chief executive while an outside investigation establishes the facts surrounding his departure; Mr. Huang resigned on November 12 after 33 years leading the company. The site’s Sunday breakdown listed 7,459 current employees, 1,406 former employees and 81,896 shareholders, all self-described, plus 63,917 other supporters; the site says affiliations are self-reported and not verified, and fake entries appeared among the names. The open letter asks for reinstatement pending an independent inquiry, or a specific explanation of why Mr. Huang’s continued absence serves the company’s interests, and disclosure of the investigation’s scope, independence and expected timeline, with an opportunity for him to respond. The board has not publicly responded to the letter, is still choosing a search firm, and an approach to an outside candidate has been reported; the company reports results on Tuesday, November 17.

 SubjectiveTechSpot — nearly 150,000 people sign a petition requesting Mr. Huang back as chief executiveThree days after Mr. Huang stepped down as Nvidia’s chief executive, a campaign to bring him back is gathering momentum: more than 150,000 people have signed an open letter urging the board to reinstate its co-founder while an independent investigation runs its course. The organisers argue he was forced out without a fair opportunity to defend himself, and ask the board to do three things: reinstate him while the investigation continues, ensure he receives a fair hearing, and publicly explain the reasoning behind his departure. By Sunday, thousands of signatories identified themselves as current employees, with tens of thousands more claiming to be shareholders; the campaign notes these are self-reported and have not been independently verified, and that the effort is not endorsed by the company or by Mr. Huang himself. The chief financial officer has taken over as interim chief executive, and a longtime director has become the board’s chair. For now the board has announced no change to its succession plans; the next major event is Tuesday’s quarterly earnings report, whose results cover the period when Mr. Huang was fully in charge.

 SubjectiveWCCFTech — Mr. Huang considers returning, allies assemble a lobbying effort, and the petition crosses 156,000Mr. Huang has discussed with close confidants the possibility of his comeback, according to a report the account cites, and allies in Silicon Valley are setting up a lobbying effort urging the board to reinstate the former chief executive. Shareholders were pressuring the board to keep the door open for Mr. Huang, with two fund managers spearheading the effort. Mr. Huang is still facing an internal investigation into a reported relationship, in the account’s telling.  SubjectiveKuCoin News — the resignation sparks a petition count of 151,083, with 80,205 shareholdersAs of November 15, the petition website calling for the board to reinstate Mr. Huang as chief executive continues to gain momentum: 151,083 individuals have signed, including 7,380 current employees, 1,381 former employees, and 80,205 shareholders, according to a financial news report the account cites. Notable public figures are listed among the signers. The company announced on November 12 that Mr. Huang had resigned as chief executive, effective immediately, ending his 33-year leadership of the company he co-founded. Organisers and signatories express concern that he may have been forced to step down without due process or sufficient opportunity to defend himself, and urge the board to provide clarification; the core demands are reinstatement pending an independent investigation to establish the facts, and, if removal is sustained, an evidence-based justification. The letter states that 33 years of leadership does not exempt a person from accountability, but that accountability requires evidence and due process. The website states the campaign is independent and has not been endorsed by the company or by Mr. Huang personally.

 SubjectiveLe Monde — the November 14 demonstrations in Paris and Lyon, diverse but determined crowdsAcross France on Saturday, November 14, demonstrations brought together a range of demands, from protecting children and increasing wages to providing more resources for education, continuing high school blockades and protesting police violence. According to the Interior Ministry, 106,000 people marched, including 24,000 in Paris, a sharp drop from previous weeks. A youth coalition of student unions claimed 200,000 demonstrators nationwide, with nearly 100,000 in the capital. Yellow Vest activists staged their fifth act against the high cost of living. The focus for many protesters was the bill called a licence to kill by its critics, scheduled to be examined by the Senate on November 19; the bill aims to introduce a presumption of self-defence after a police officer or gendarme fires a weapon.

 SubjectiveParticle News — France’s protests continue as the police firearms bill heads to the SenateThe nationwide demonstrations ran for a fifth Saturday in a row on November 14, and the Interior Ministry put turnout at about 106,000 people, including roughly 24,000 in Paris, while organisers gave higher estimates. The bill approved by the lower house would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they fire their weapons, a legal change critics call by a name the account quotes. The movement now unites high-school students, trade unions, Yellow Vest activists and child-protection campaigners demanding better school conditions, higher pay and relief from the rising cost of living. Senate consideration of the measure is set to follow union plans for a nationwide strike on Tuesday, November 17, and the account records that unions rejected a 0.6 percent minimum-wage offer.

### Sunday&rsquo;s Recovery Reaches Nearly 1,600 Cancellations by 1000 Against 875 Down at Dawn, Bahrain Answers Its Morning in Writing&mdash;Resolution 2817, Article 51 and a Red Line&mdash;While Washington Files No Word on the Radar, and Alaska&rsquo;s Count Stands at 140,637 to 129,424 With the Next Count Due Monday

Filed as: Edition No. 50 — The Midday Watch · 2026-11-15T12:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-15-midday-watch.html

The Midday File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Sunday’s Recovery Reaches Nearly 1,600 Cancellations by 1000 Against 875 Down at Dawn, Bahrain Answers Its Morning in Writing—Resolution 2817, Article 51 and a Red Line—While Washington Files No Word on the Radar, and Alaska’s Count Stands at 140,637 to 129,424 With the Next Count Due Monday

 The midday file: a recovery counted at nearly 1,600 against 875 expected, and a promise that divides between tonight and tomorrow; a kingdom that answered its morning with intercepts, a resolution and a red line, against a radar claim no capital has confirmed; a count that did not move, printed to the vote; a spokesman’s two sentences in Moscow; a petition counted past 135,000 and questioned in the same accounts; and a Sunday with no session, read in the one market that never closes.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1200 ET, Sunday, November 15, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 49, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, from Edition No. 48, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, from Edition No. 47, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Saturday, and from Edition No. 46, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Saturday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midday figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midday in Brief: A Recovery Counted Higher Than the Dawn Expected, a Statement From Manama, and a Count That Did Not Move

The midday’s corrections run in one direction: Sunday is costing more flights than the dawn file carried, and the morning’s other files gained statements rather than settlements. Nearly 1,600 flights had been cancelled and 2,570 delayed by 1000 on Sunday in the tracker’s figures, in the day-three account filed below, against 875 of Sunday’s flights already cancelled in the overnight accounts and 1,390 cancelled on Sunday morning in the warnings account filed below; more than 17,000 flights have been scrubbed since Friday, in the day-three account. In Bahrain’s file, the kingdom spoke twice on Sunday morning—the Defence Force on intercepts, the Foreign Ministry on law—in the Bahrain account and the ministry account filed below, while the Guards’ claim of a radar hit at Al-Riffa stands without an American or Bahraini confirmation at 1200. In Alaska, no new count came on Sunday morning; the state’s Saturday-afternoon report stands at 140,637 to 129,424, and the race stands uncalled. In Moscow, the Kremlin’s spokesman answered the European question in two words and the European prospect in one sentence, both filed below. The markets have no Sunday session; the reading is Friday’s closes, the weekend’s one open market, and a week of dates.

The Airlines at Midday: Nearly 1,600 Cancelled by 1000, a Router Named in the Cause File, and a Promise in Two Versions

The recovery’s shape at midday is a system declared stable and a schedule still being rationed. The Administration said late Saturday that the system is stable and returning to normal operations, and its dashboard on Sunday morning reported no active en-route events, in the national account filed below, which records that local traffic-management programs remain possible later today in eight named areas, among them Dallas-Fort Worth, Denver, Houston, Seattle and San Francisco, as airport and route contingencies and not another nationwide stop; Kennedy and O’Hare each reported general delays of fifteen minutes or less on Sunday morning, in the same account. The cost stands against that stability in the tracker’s figures: at 0800, JetBlue had cancelled 27 percent of its Sunday operation, the highest share among the large carriers; American had scrapped 368 flights, the most of any carrier; Delta and Southwest had each cancelled more than 170, and United about 100, in the day-three account above. American’s chief customer officer called the disruption among the most significant operational impacts the carrier has experienced, in a Saturday-evening letter in the same account; American said all its planned cancellations for Saturday night and Sunday had been completed, with individual flights still liable to cancel, and Delta advised passengers with flexible plans to move their travel to Monday, in the same account and the warnings account above. Fewer than 30 flights for Monday had been cancelled by Sunday morning, in the day-three account.

The official statements at midday divide on the day’s one promise, and the cause file gained its most specific account. Administrator Bedford’s Saturday words stand in the day-three account: the airline partners believe they will be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. Secretary Duffy’s Sunday words stand in the scramble account filed below: things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow. The desk prints the two versions apart in the Cocked Hat; the evening collection will read the day against both. On cause, the preliminary investigation points to work by the contractor L3Harris during a routine upgrade from copper wiring to fiber: a newly installed or modified router began flooding other routers with data, disrupting communications and radar information at the control centers, and investigators are determining whether the underlying problem was equipment failure or contractor or installer error, in the national account above. The contractor’s Saturday statement stands in the same account: more than 70 percent of the planned conversion from copper to fiber is complete, and the company is supporting the investigation. The Secretary’s Saturday sentence stands beside it, in the day-three account: the system did not meet the moment, the contractor did not meet the moment, or the equipment did not. Saturday’s corrected totals stand where the morning left them—more than 6,400 cancelled and 8,000 delayed in the tracker’s late count, against nearly 6,500 cancelled in the midnight edition’s—and Friday’s at about 9,200 cancelled and 7,500 delayed, in the national account; roughly 15,600 were cancelled on the two days together before Sunday’s are counted.

The Count at Midday: No New Count on Sunday Morning, 157 Short of a Majority by the Desk’s Arithmetic, and a Winner Listed in One Place

Alaska’s Senate count at midday is Saturday afternoon’s report, unchanged, and the desk prints it whole. The state’s unofficial summary, timed 1515 on Saturday, gives Ms. Peltola 140,637 votes, 49.94 percent; Senator Sullivan 129,424, 45.96 percent; Mr. Heikes 6,002; Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. 4,652; and write-ins 872, on 281,587 votes in the race, with 283,618 ballots cast and all 401 precincts reported, in the state’s report filed below. The lead is 11,213. A majority of the reported vote is 140,794; Ms. Peltola stands 157 votes short of it, by the desk’s arithmetic on the state’s figures. The Press’s count at 0049 UTC on Sunday carries the same figures, estimates 97 percent of the vote counted, and lists the race not called, in the count account filed below, which prices the last batch: 4,219 votes added since the Press’s Saturday 0500 UTC count, 2,397 of them for Ms. Peltola and 1,596 for Senator Sullivan. The state’s dashboard rounds Ms. Peltola to 50.1 percent because unresolved write-ins are excluded from that display calculation, in the lead account filed below, and one results tracker prints the same 50.1 and marks her the winner, in the tracker account filed below; the desk prints the listing and the non-call side by side, as it has printed them all week. Ms. Peltola declared victory on Saturday at the earlier lead of 10,412, in the declaration account filed below; Senator Sullivan has not conceded and has not posted publicly since November 4, in the same account. The next count is due Monday; overseas ballots may arrive through Wednesday, November 18, when the ranked-choice tabulation is scheduled if no candidate holds a majority, and certification is targeted for November 25. A Peltola seat makes the caucus 56; a Sullivan seat, 55.

Bahrain at Midday: Two Alerts, an Intercept Claim From the Defence Force, a Foreign Ministry Statement, and No Word From Washington

Manama’s morning gained its official paper at midday, and the paper names names the alerts did not. The Interior Ministry’s two alerts went out at 0432 and 0650 Bahrain time, urging citizens and residents to remain calm, proceed to the nearest safe location and follow news through official channels, and naming no threat, source or target, in the Bahrain account at the top of this report; an agency journalist in Manama reported sirens and explosions at about 0400, and residents a second series at about 0630. The Defence Force then said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks before they reached their targets, and that all units remain at the highest level of readiness, in the same account. The Foreign Ministry’s statement, in the ministry account above, condemns the continued attacks in the strongest terms: drones intercepted and destroyed on Sunday, and two more on Friday; a resumption of aggression in blatant disregard of international law and the Charter; a flagrant violation of Security Council Resolution 2817, which condemned Iranian attacks on Bahrain and its neighbours and demanded their immediate cessation; Bahrain’s inherent right, individual and collective, to self-defence under Article 51, exercised in coordination with the Gulf Cooperation Council, whose joint defence agreement treats an attack on one member as an attack on all; a call, from a member of the Council, for the Council to condemn the attacks and take decisive measures to ensure full compliance; the rejection of the Guards’ pretexts; and the sentence that the kingdom’s security is a red line. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt issued condemnations of their own on Sunday, in the accounts filed below.

Against the paper stand the claim and the silence. The Guards say six drones of their Aerospace Force targeted the American air-defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base, in a second phase of retaliation, carried by the state broadcaster’s channel, by Fars and by Press TV, in the Bahrain account above and in the alert account filed below. No damage and no casualties have been reported, and neither Washington nor Manama has confirmed a hit, in both accounts. Central Command, which denied Friday’s claim in claim-and-fact form—two drones launched, both shot down, no injuries, no damage—has filed no word on Sunday’s claim in any account the desk read by 1200, and the desk records the silence as a fact of the file, not as an answer. Tehran’s answer to Manama’s Article 51 is its own Article 51: its Foreign Ministry’s spokesman told a news conference that attacks on Iran’s neighbours were justified in self-defence, and accused the Gulf states of helping Washington strike his country, in the intercepts account filed below, which also dates the resolution Manama cites: adopted March 11, 2026, by thirteen votes to none with China and Russia abstaining, on a Bahraini text with 135 co-sponsors. The President’s Saturday condition stands in the Bahrain account: he might hold off on attacking Iran if there were no new provocations from Tehran or the Houthis, and he would maintain the naval blockade. Whether Sunday’s claimed strike is a provocation in that sentence’s meaning has not been said by Washington by 1200. The seven conditions, the letter to Congress and the strait figures stand where the week left them.

Dublin and Shenzhen at Midday: ‘No, Not Yet,’ a Sentence About Force, and a Departure on Monday

Europe’s file at midday is two answers from one spokesman. Asked by the TASS agency whether the negotiators appointed by the Union have attempted to contact Russia, spokesman Peskov answered: “No, not yet,” in the contact account filed below, which records the Dublin form the question was about—the institutions and the five countries, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, Italy and Poland, with the Commission and the Council. In an interview with a Vesti correspondent, the same spokesman said that in the absence of a negotiated solution with Europe, Russia will have to achieve its objectives by force, and that if the Union does not want peace there is no point in discussing a settlement or a European security framework, in the force account and the wire account filed below. The two answers stand against the standing American position in the file: the White House’s deputy press secretary said on November 13 that the American delegation at Abu Dhabi ensured Europe will be included in future talks, in the assessment filed below, which also carries President Zelenskyy’s November 14 statement that the American delegation at Abu Dhabi proposed that Ukraine gain NATO membership in exchange for a Ukrainian withdrawal from the entirety of the Donbas, and the report that the Russian delegation circulated an unofficial paper of demands at those talks. No date for a next round, and no contact, stands in the midday file.

Shenzhen gained no third confirmation and gained an itinerary. The meeting of the three presidents on Thursday, November 19 stands confirmed by the White House on Friday and by the Kremlin on Saturday, and unconfirmed by its host, in the meeting account filed below and the week’s file; China’s Foreign Ministry’s Friday sentence, that it is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state, stands unamended at 1200. The President travels to Manila on Monday for the ASEAN meetings and continues to Shenzhen, where he is due from November 17 through 19, in the week’s accounts. The agenda split stands: nuclear arms and Iran in the American telling, Ukraine off the trilateral agenda in the same telling and on it in the Kremlin aide’s. Nothing in the midday file moves either sentence.

Nvidia and the Markets at Midday: A Counter at 135,468 and Questioned in the Same Accounts, and a Sunday Read in One Open Market

Nvidia’s file at midday is a number and a challenge to the number. The petition’s counter showed 135,468 signatures at 0037 on Sunday, in the petition account filed below, which classifies 6,776 of the signers as current employees, 1,267 as former employees and 73,181 as shareholders, and records that those affiliations have not been independently verified and that neither the company nor Mr. Huang endorses the campaign. A second Sunday account puts the count at more than 120,000, in the resignation account filed below. A third, in the finance account filed below, puts it at nearly 130,000 on Saturday evening and prints the challenge in the same file: the site lacks real-name verification, the signatures are hard to verify, and a company vice president, Mr. Catanzaro, has said publicly that he never signed and that his name was used without his consent. The petition’s asks stand in all three accounts: reinstatement while an independent investigation establishes the facts, the investigation’s scope, independence and timetable made public, a substantive opportunity to respond, and, if the board insists he leave, a specific, evidence-backed explanation. The board’s succession file gained one sentence over the weekend: it is choosing a search firm and has not formally engaged any potential candidates, in the Monday-prep account filed below. No finding has been made by the board, by any committee or by any court on any allegation in this file. Earnings stand on Tuesday, November 17, at about 1620, with the call at 1700 in one account and at 1320 and 1400 Pacific in another—the same hour, printed two ways; consensus revenue stands at $108.9 billion against the company’s outlook of $108.0 billion, in the same account.

The markets’ reading at midday is a reading of a closed week and an open one. Sunday has no cash session. Friday’s closes stand: the S&P 500 at 7,561.67, down 0.40 percent; the Nasdaq Composite at 25,136.27, down 0.91; the Dow at 52,347.60, up 0.10; the ten-year yield at 5.15 percent; the dollar index at 103.41. The one market that trades on Sunday moved all weekend, and the desk prints its readings apart: $64,830, down 2.97 percent on the day and 8.60 on five sessions, at 0544 UTC in the daily brief filed below; a low of $62,006 overnight, the lowest since July, and $65,570 at 0845 and $64,770 at 1000, in the bitcoin account filed below; and $65,714 at 0420, after a three-month low on Saturday, in the Monday-prep account filed below, which also carries the Federal Reserve’s November 13 finding that 87 percent of the market contacts it surveyed named artificial intelligence a major risk to the financial system, up from 50 percent in the spring and 30 percent a year earlier. Futures reopen at 1800 today; Friday’s futures closes stand at minus 0.42 percent for the S&P 500 and minus 1.23 for the Nasdaq 100, in the same account. The week’s calendar is dated in every file: retail sales and Nvidia on Tuesday, the October meeting minutes on Wednesday, the Anthropic listing on Thursday.

France and Spain at Midday: A Fifth Saturday Closed at Two Counts, a Bill Gone to the Senate, and a Mean That Moved One Tenth

France’s fifth Saturday closed, and Sunday’s accounts price its calm and its counts apart. The Interior Ministry’s figures stand: 106,000 demonstrators nationwide, 24,000 of them in Paris, down from 146,000 and 46,000 the Saturday before, and 219 detained, in the midnight edition’s file and in the rally account filed below, which records the authorities’ reading that Saturday stayed largely calm and turnout declined. The organisers’ figures stand beside them: about 200,000 nationwide and almost 100,000 in the capital, in the week’s accounts. The contested police bill—the measure giving officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms, passed by the lower house—now heads to the Senate, in the Senate account filed below. The unions’ Tuesday strike stands, called after the government’s 0.6 percent minimum-wage promise was rejected as crumbs, in both accounts; Tuesday is also the eighth anniversary of the Yellow Vest movement, whose adherents say they will mark it on roundabouts and toll booths all over France, in the rally account, and a sixth Saturday, Acte VI, is called for November 21, in the week’s accounts.

Spain’s campaign spent its first Sunday with its mean nearly still. The mean of the latest study from each institute, dated November 15 and now across sixteen institutes, stands at Popular Party 31.4 percent, Socialists 26.9, Vox 19.1, Frente Amplio 6.3 and ERC 2.5, in the campaign account filed below: against the fifteen-institute mean the midday edition printed on Saturday, the only movement is Frente Amplio down one tenth. The polls still do not meet—the state survey’s Socialist lead and the 40dB survey’s two-point gap stand in the file where the week left them—and polls may publish until November 23. Spain votes on November 29.

The Afternoon Ahead: An Evening Collection at 1800 and a Week Written in Dates

The afternoon’s measures are the recovery’s and the silence’s. Sunday’s cancellation total will be read against the Administrator’s close-of-business promise and the Secretary’s tomorrow, and against the nearly 1,600 counted by 1000. Any American word on the Al-Riffa claim, and any Bahraini report of damage, will enter the file when it stands. The week ahead is dated: the President departs Monday; Alaska’s next count comes Monday and its tabulation Wednesday, the day the APEC leaders meet in Shenzhen and the Federal Reserve publishes its October minutes; Nvidia reports Tuesday after the close; Alaska’s certification target and the expenditures report share November 25; the European Council takes up Ukraine’s financing on November 26 and 27; Spain votes November 29; Mr. Huang’s interview stands dated December 1; the Federal Reserve decides December 8 and 9. This paper’s Sunday Review of Reviews stands filed separately, ahead of the day’s watches. The Evening Watch collects at 1800.

The Cocked Hat

Where the midday’s bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On Sunday’s cost by midday: 875 cancelled at dawn in the overnight file, more than 900 by late Saturday in one account, 1,390 on Sunday morning in the warnings account, 1,421 in one tracker reading, and nearly 1,600 cancelled with 2,570 delayed by 1000 in the day-three account—a rising series taken at different hours, not a disagreement about one hour. On the promise: full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday, in the Administrator’s Saturday words; fully normal tomorrow, in the Secretary’s Sunday words. On the failed thing: a router flooding other routers during a copper-to-fiber upgrade in the preliminary account, with equipment failure and installer error both open; overloaded switches and routers in the Secretary’s earlier account; and a network handling critical radio frequencies in two airline officials’ account from Saturday. On Alaska’s share: 49.94 percent on the state’s full denominator, 50.1 on the dashboard that excludes unresolved write-ins, a winner listed on one tracker, no call from the Press, and a victory declared by the candidate. On Bahrain: intercepts and destruction in the Defence Force’s account, six drones on target in the Guards’, and no confirmation of a hit from any capital; on the law, Article 51 is claimed by Manama and by Tehran in the same morning, for opposite acts. On Europe: not yet contacted, in the spokesman’s answer to TASS; included in future talks, in the White House’s November 13 sentence; and objectives by force absent a negotiated solution, in the spokesman’s interview. On the petition: 135,468 on its own counter at 0037, more than 120,000 in one Sunday account, nearly 130,000 on Saturday evening in a third, and its signatures unverifiable and at least one name used without consent, in the third account’s own file. On bitcoin: $62,006, $64,770, $64,830 and $65,714 in four readings taken at four hours of a Sunday. On France: 106,000 in the Ministry’s count and about 200,000 in the organisers’. On Spain’s Socialists: 26.9 in the sixteen-institute mean and a lead in the state survey. Inside the triangle is where the midday honestly stands.

 The Clippings Filed With This Edition

 Everything the desk read for the report above, clipped and filed as a bureau files it. Each item is stamped subjective—a source with a position, printed because it is useful—and described by what it says. The desk’s report is the only item in this edition stamped objective. 29 items.

 

 SubjectiveThe Points Guy — nearly 1,600 cancelled by 1000 Sunday, more than 17,000 scrubbed since Friday, and fewer than 30 of Monday’s downSunday was shaping up to be another rough day at airports across the country, with travellers facing a third straight day of widespread cancellations after Friday’s nationwide ground stop. As of 10 a.m. Eastern on Sunday, nearly 1,600 flights had been cancelled, according to FlightAware, and an additional 2,570 had already encountered delays. All told, more than 17,000 flights have been scrubbed since Friday. As of 8 a.m., JetBlue had cancelled 27 percent of its operation for the day, the highest cancellation rate of any American carrier on Sunday; American had scrapped more departures than any airline, 368 flights; Delta and Southwest had each cancelled more than 170, and United about 100. American’s chief customer officer, in a letter to customers on Saturday evening, called the disruption among the most significant operational impacts the carrier has experienced and said it expected disruption throughout the weekend as it reset the airline. Delta urged passengers with flexible plans to consider postponing travel until Monday. Administrator Bedford had said the disruptions were expected to begin easing by Sunday evening: based on everything heard from the airline partners, they believe they will be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. As of Sunday morning, fewer than 30 flights for Monday had been cancelled. The stop was ordered late Friday after a communications outage affecting air traffic control, as crews upgraded equipment amid a switch from copper wiring to fiber at one facility. Secretary Duffy said at a Saturday press conference that this was a system that did not meet the moment, that the contractor did not meet the moment, or the equipment did not, and caused the outages. The account records that passengers whose flights are cancelled or significantly delayed are entitled to a refund if they choose not to travel, regardless of the reason, and that because the disruption was due to issues outside the airlines’ control, carriers are unlikely to reimburse hotel, ground transportation and meal costs.

 SubjectiveUSA Today — the system stable, no active en-route events, the router in the preliminary account, and the contractor’s statementAir travel remained disrupted on the morning of November 15 after more than 15,000 flights were cancelled in the last two days following the nationwide ground stop, but officials say the system is stable and schedules should largely return to normal by the night of November 15. The Administration said on X late on November 14 that the system is stable and it is returning to normal operations. In all, 875 flights scheduled for Sunday were already cancelled, the tracker said, and another 1,904 delayed. As of the morning of November 15, the Administration’s National Airspace System dashboard reported no active en-route events, a strong indication the communications failure is no longer constraining the national system; local traffic management programs are still possible later today, including in the Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio, Denver, Houston, San Diego, Seattle and San Francisco areas, as airport and route-specific contingencies, not another nationwide ground stop. Kennedy and Chicago O’Hare were each reporting general arrival and departure delays of fifteen minutes or less. November 14 was extremely rough: the tracker counted more than 6,400 cancellations and 8,000 delays by late in the day. On November 13 about 9,200 flights were cancelled and 7,500 delayed after essentially all departures were halted for nearly five hours; roughly 15,600 flights were cancelled Friday and Saturday alone, before Sunday’s are included. Secretary Duffy said November 14 that the preliminary investigation points to work by the contractor L3Harris during a routine upgrade from copper wiring to fiber: a newly installed or modified router began flooding other routers with data, disrupting communications and radar information at control centers, and investigators are determining whether the underlying problem was equipment failure or contractor or installer error. L3Harris, which manages the telecommunications infrastructure supporting about 45,000 daily flights and connecting more than 4,400 facilities, said it has completed more than 70 percent of the planned conversion from copper wires to a fiber optic system and is supporting the investigation to understand the conditions that led to the November 13 ground stop. Administrator Bedford has said the outdated copper wires should be completely replaced by September 2027.

 SubjectiveThe Travel — 1,390 cancelled on Sunday morning, American at 368, and warnings standing for 21 airportsCancellations continued into Sunday, with the total nearing the 1,400 mark on the morning of November 15 after cancellations on Friday and Saturday exceeded 15,000. American had the most cancelled flights among the 1,390 total, with 368 cancelled affecting at least 10 percent of its flights, according to the tracker. Dallas-Fort Worth, Chicago O’Hare and New York Kennedy were the hubs facing the most cancellations, with triple-digit cancellations. American and Delta are among the carriers to issue updates: both confirmed cancellations are expected to continue into Sunday, though they have made improvements in getting passengers back on flights, and major airlines extended flexible rebooking offers as cancellations trickled into Sunday. American said in an update on Saturday evening that its recovery continues to move forward, that all planned cancellations for that night and the next day had been completed, though some individual flights may still be cancelled as it works to fully restore the operation, and that customers travelling that night or the next day should continue to check their flight status before heading to the airport. Delta encouraged passengers to book flights as of Monday as the carrier continues to restore its system.

 SubjectiveVidia News — more than 900 of Sunday’s cancelled by late Saturday, 6,400 on Saturday and 9,200 on FridayMore than 900 flights scheduled for Sunday in the United States had been cancelled by late Saturday as airlines continued to recover from the nationwide ground stop. The tracker recorded 910 cancellations for Sunday, with the figure rising. More than 6,400 flights were cancelled on Saturday, following about 9,200 on Friday; the order halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours on Friday. Administrator Bedford said he did think the worst was behind them, but added that a significant amount of recovery work remained, and that based on everything heard from the airline partners, they believed they would be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. Secretary Duffy said the disruption began during work to replace old copper telecommunications lines with fibre-optic cables at a facility. The Administration said it ordered the ground stop as a safety measure after communications problems affected 17 of its 22 en-route air traffic control centres.

 SubjectiveThe Washington Post, carried by Wallhop — the scramble to normal by the evening, and the Secretary’s Sunday version of the promiseAirlines scrambled Sunday to return flight schedules to normal by the evening, two days after the nationwide ground stop triggered widespread cancellations and delays across the United States. While thousands of flights were disrupted over the weekend, with over a thousand more cancellations reported Sunday, airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crews, after officials expressed confidence that the worst of the disruption is over. “We’re going to see things come back to normal today, but probably fully normal tomorrow,” Secretary Duffy told a Sunday program. Administrator Bedford said airlines expect they will be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday. The tracker reported that more than 6,600 flights within, into or out of the United States were cancelled on Saturday, with at least 1,300 additional cancellations recorded early Sunday. American said all planned cancellations for Saturday night and Sunday had been completed, although some individual flights could still be cancelled as it works to restore operations. Delta said it was continuing to restore its operations but advising customers with flexible travel plans to move their flights to Monday or later because of the potential for further disruption on Sunday. The ground stop on Friday afternoon marked the first time flights across the entire country had been halted since January 2023, when a computer system failure affected the pilot alerting system; in the latest stop, flights were halted for more than four hours before restrictions were lifted around 2015 on Friday. Secretary Duffy said the outage was believed to have been caused by problems during maintenance at a remote site, where a contractor was replacing old copper telecommunications lines with fiber-optic cables.

 SubjectiveDINA — the lead at 11,213, the dashboard’s 50.1 explained, and the result not certifiedMs. Peltola now leads Senator Sullivan by 11,213 first-choice votes, in an update the account presents exactly as a major update to the unofficial first-choice count: the Press and most major national decision desks had not declared a winner when the report was published, the result is not certified, and the account is not presenting the count as a projection or certification. The latest reported numbers are Ms. Peltola 140,637, 49.94 percent, and Senator Sullivan 129,424, 45.96 percent, with Mr. Heikes at 6,002 and Mr. Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. at 4,652. The state’s public dashboard may round Ms. Peltola to 50.1 percent because unresolved write-ins are excluded from that display calculation.  SubjectiveBallot Brief — the Press’s count at 0049 UTC: 4,219 new votes, 49.9 percent, and not calledThe Press’s count as of November 15, 2026, at 0049 UTC lists the Alaska Senate race as not called and estimates 97 percent of the vote counted. The count stands at 281,587 votes: Ms. Peltola 140,637, 49.9 percent; Senator Sullivan 129,424, 46.0 percent; Mr. Heikes 6,002, 2.1 percent; Mr. Sullivan Jr. 4,652, 1.7 percent; and write-in votes 872, 0.3 percent. It records what is not known: the Press has not called the race, the account makes no projection, about 3 percent of the vote is estimated not yet counted, and the count may change.

 SubjectiveUS News Pulse — Ms. Peltola declares victory at 10,412, the race not officially called, and Senator Sullivan not concededMs. Peltola declared victory in Alaska’s Senate race early on Saturday, November 14, after a new batch of ballots widened her lead to 10,412 votes, telling supporters there is no path left for her opponent. Her campaign announced it as the latest results showed her ahead 138,240 to 127,828, about 49.8 percent to 46.2, with roughly 95 to 96 percent counted. She stood about 445 votes short of the 50 percent majority that would avoid a ranked-choice tabulation in that count. The race has not been officially called, and Senator Sullivan has not conceded and has not posted publicly since November 4. A prediction market called Ms. Peltola the winner on Saturday, and one report says a network has called the race for her; the Press, however, has not officially called it. The declaration followed a count that had stood days earlier at a lead of just 626 votes, 102,701 to 102,075, with 394 of the state’s 401 precincts reporting. The next milestone is November 18, when the ranked-choice tabulation is scheduled if she finishes below 50 percent, and state certification is targeted for November 25.
